scope: The two opposite cluster exponentials are inverse matrices, for any finite index set. This supplies the cancellation in the coupled-cluster similarity transform.
The exponential of a sum of cluster generators acting on disjoint fragments is the Kronecker product of the fragment exponentials, even for approximate fragment amplitudes.

For independent fragments and a product reference determinant, the similarity-transformed Hamiltonian is the sum of the individual transformed operators lifted to the composite. The projected coupled-cluster energies add exactly.
A positive-semidefinite energy lower bound and a saturating product eigenvector certify that independent fragments have additive ground energies, including minimization over entangled states.
For L identical independent copies, exact ground energy and projected coupled-cluster energy are each L times their fragment value. The cluster amplitudes may be approximate.

Lee et al., discussion at Fig. 3A. For L independent copies of a fixed finite fragment, assume the fragment calculation reaches absolute error δ in at most C δ⁻ᵇ work. Solving at δ = ε/L gives total absolute energy error ≤ ε with at most (C+1)Lᵇ⁺¹ ε⁻ᵇ work, counting one energy addition per copy. The fragment convergence rate is an explicit hypothesis.
